subtitle: Bhutapala’s Stone Mansion and the Merchants of the Western Sea

panels.shot: epic wide-angle of Karla’s great chaitya hall interior seen from the entrance, dim light washing over stone ribs and the silent stupa
panels.action: The vast rock-cut hall of Karla looms in solemn grandeur, its vaulted stone ribs arcing over the central stupa like a fossilized ship, bathed in soft, slanting light.

dialogue.text: In the western hills of Jambudvipa, merchants and monks carved Karla’s great chaitya, where Bhutapala the banker dared call his stone mansion the most excellent of all.

i18n.hi: जंबूद्वीप के पश्चिमी पहाड़ों में व्यापारियों और भिक्षुओं ने कार्ला का महान चैत्य तराशा, जहाँ सेठ भूतपाल ने अपने पत्थर-महल को सबमें श्रेष्ठ कहा।

panels.shot: wide aerial over the Western Ghats with a distant hint of the Konkan coast, monsoon clouds rolling, caravan trail snaking below
panels.action: Bhutapala stands tiny on a ridge path in the Western Ghats, wrapped in a merchant’s cloak, watching caravans of oxen and men wind through the misty passes toward the distant sea.

dialogue.text: In the first century of the Common Era, the Western Ghats guarded the road between the Deccan plateau and the Arabian Sea, where ships waited for men like Bhutapala.

i18n.hi: समय था सामान्य युग की पहली सदी का, पश्चिमी घाट देक्कन से अरब सागर तक की राह की रखवाली कर रहे थे, जहाँ भूतपाल जैसे लोगों के लिए जहाज़ ठहरे रहते।

panels.shot: intimate mid-shot inside a bustling guild hall, low-angle showing carved wooden beams and hanging oil lamps over traders at work
panels.action: Bhutapala, dignified and composed, sits among other guild elders in a crowded hall, counting punch-marked coins as scribes record loans on palm leaves under flickering lamps.

dialogue.text: In distant Vaijayanti, Bhutapala was a setthi, a banker among merchants, weaving credit and trust across workshops, caravans and sea routes.

i18n.hi: दूर वैजयन्ती में भूतपाल एक सेठी था, व्यापारियों का बैंकर, जो करघों, कारवाँ और समुद्री रास्तों पर भरोसा और उधार की जाल बुनता था।

panels.shot: wide seaside shot from behind Bhutapala, overlooking a crowded western port with wooden ships, warehouses and monk-beggars among traders
panels.action: Bhutapala overlooks a lively harbor where broad-hulled ships lie at anchor, monks in simple robes walk between bales of goods as sailors load jars and textiles aboard.

dialogue.text: The monsoon winds brought ships from across the western sea, and merchants met monks on the wharves, where talk of profit mingled with talk of merit.

i18n.hi: बरसाती पवनें पश्चिमी सागर पार से जहाज़ लातीं, घाटों पर व्यापारी और भिक्षु मिलते, जहाँ लाभ की बातें और पुण्य की बातें साथ-साथ गूंजतीं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a shaded verandah at Karla hillside, monks and merchants seated together, stony cliff-face behind them
panels.action: On a ledge below the cliff at Karla, Bhutapala sits opposite senior Buddhist monks, listening intently as they gesture toward the rock wall that rises above their gathering.

dialogue.text: Among those hills near Lonavala, monks had begun to carve dwellings and prayer halls into stone, seeking a refuge for the sangha and its supporters.

i18n.hi: लोणावला के पास उन पहाड़ियों में भिक्षु पत्थर में ही विहार और प्रार्थना-सभाएँ काट रहे थे, संघ और उसके सहायक के लिए आसरा खोजते हुए।

panels.shot: low-angle wide of the cliff face being marked, figures tiny against raw rock, chalk lines tracing the outline of a vast hall
panels.action: Artisans stand on bamboo scaffolds pressed to the cliff, sketching white outlines of pillars and vaults while Bhutapala watches from below, hands folded, imagining the future hall.

dialogue.text: Karla’s Cave 8 would be no small shelter, but a vast chaitya hall, cut from living rock with ribs of stone echoing a wooden roof and a forest of pillars.

i18n.hi: कार्ला की गुफा ८ छोटी शरण नहीं, बल्कि विशाल चैत्य-सभागार बनने वाली थी, जीवित चट्टान में काटी हुई, पत्थर की पसलियाँ लकड़ी की छत और स्तंभों के जंगल की गूँज।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-shot inside an early stage of excavation, dust hanging in the air as hammer and chisel freeze mid-swing
panels.action: Within the half-carved cavern, craftsmen strike iron chisels against the rock, stone dust clouding the air as the outline of future pillars and the central stupa slowly emerges.

dialogue.text: Year after year, the hall grew under calloused hands, funded by merchants, bankers and guilds whose names would later cling to the stone.

i18n.hi: साल दर साल कठोर हथेलियों के नीचे वह सभागार बढ़ता गया, व्यापारियों, सेठों और श्रोतों के धन से, जिनके नाम बाद में पत्थर से चिपक गए।

panels.shot: solemn mid-shot in the almost finished hall, side-on view of Bhutapala touching a smooth pillar, artisans in the background fixing wooden roof elements
panels.action: Bhutapala walks between newly carved pillars, fingers tracing the smooth stone as workers fit curved wooden pieces along the vaulted ceiling above him.

dialogue.speaker: bhutapala_and_the_karla_donors
dialogue.text: Let this be a mansion of merit, strong as the rock itself.

i18n.hi: यह पुण्य का महल हो, चट्टान जितना अटल।

panels.shot: close-up on a pillar base where a stonecutter kneels, carving Brahmi letters, Bhutapala looming in soft focus behind
panels.action: A stonecutter carves neat Brahmi letters into the base of a pillar while Bhutapala stands nearby, dictating the words that will proclaim his gift to the sangha.

dialogue.text: In his inscription, Bhutapala of Vaijayanti called the completed chaitya a rock mansion, declaring it the most excellent in Jambudvipa, a proud boast in stone.

i18n.hi: अपनी लेख में वैजयन्ती के भूतपाल ने बने हुए चैत्य को पत्थर का महल कहा, और उसे जंबूद्वीप में सबसे उत्कृष्ट घोषित किया — पत्थर में खुदी हुई गर्वीली शेखी।

panels.shot: wide interior of the hall with rows of pillars, some bases highlighted, various donors gathered around, mix of dress styles
panels.action: Different merchants and guild members stand by selected pillars, indicating which ones they have funded, as monks observe and the central stupa rises in quiet majesty beyond.

dialogue.text: Many pillars bore donor names: bankers, caravan leaders, guilds and men whose wealth flowed along the roads and sea lanes of the western Deccan.

i18n.hi: कई स्तंभों पर दाताओं के नाम थे: सेठ, कारवाँ-नायक, श्रोते और वे लोग जिनकी संपत्ति पश्चिमी देक्कन की सड़कों और समुद्री मार्गों पर बहती थी।

panels.shot: focused mid-shot on one pillar with a foreign-looking donor, modest but distinct clothing, stonecutter inscribing the word ‘Yavana’ in Brahmi
panels.action: Beside a pillar, a bearded donor with distinct foreign-style cloak stands quietly as his identity as a Yavana from Denukakata is carved in Brahmi by the artisan at his feet.

dialogue.text: Some pillars spoke of Yavana donors from Denukakata, men of western origin living within Indian ports, sharing in the same quest for merit.

i18n.hi: कुछ स्तंभों ने देनुककट से आए यवन दाताओं की बात कही, पश्चिमी मूल के वे लोग जो भारतीय बंदरगाहों में बसकर उसी पुण्य की तलाश में थे।

panels.shot: tight shot on faces of different donors and monks in lamplight, diverse features and garments, all turned toward the stupa
panels.action: Merchants of varied appearance, including the Yavana, stand shoulder to shoulder with monks, the stupa glowing in the lamplight as they silently pay respect.

dialogue.text: At Karla, shared devotion crossed the lines of city, language and origin, binding local traders and western-born Yavanas in the same stone corridor of faith.

i18n.hi: कार्ला में साझा भक्ति ने नगर, भाषा और जन्म-भूमि की रेखाएँ लाँघ दीं, देसी व्यापारियों और पश्चिमजन्मे यवनों को एक ही पत्थर की श्रद्धा-गलियारे में बाँध दिया।

panels.shot: wide-angle view of the completed hall from the entrance, rows of inscribed pillars leading to the stupa, wooden ribs vivid above
panels.action: The finished chaitya stretches before the viewer, pillars aligned like a stone forest, inscriptions at their bases, and the surviving wooden beams arching above toward the central stupa.

dialogue.text: By the mid-first century, Karla’s hall stood among the largest of its kind, its stone ribs and inscribed pillars sheltering chanting voices from rain and sun.

i18n.hi: पहली सदी के मध्य तक कार्ला का सभागार अपने तरह के सबसे बड़े हलों में था, पत्थर की पसलियाँ और लिखे स्तंभ बारिश और धूप से जपती आवाजों को थामे हुए।

panels.shot: mid-shot decades later, monks and lay visitors inside the dim hall, older pillars bearing new small inscriptions scratched nearby
panels.action: Time has passed; monks lead lay visitors around the hall as fresh, smaller inscriptions appear on some surfaces, showing that new gifts have been added over the years.

dialogue.text: The hall did not freeze in Bhutapala’s time. Later donors came, adding their words and gifts, extending the life of the space beyond one generation.

i18n.hi: सभा-स्थल भूतपाल के समय पर ही स्थिर नहीं हुआ, बाद के दाता आए, अपनी बातें और उपहार जोड़े, और इस जगह की उम्र एक पीढ़ी से आगे बढ़ा दी।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle outside the cave entrance, royal entourage approaching, guards and horses against the cliff
panels.action: A later royal entourage approaches Karla’s entrance, banners fluttering as attendants and guards escort a noble figure associated with the Western Satraps toward the sacred site.

dialogue.text: In time, the inscriptions record gifts from Ushavadata of the Western Satraps, showing that even new powers of the region honored older Buddhist sanctuaries.

i18n.hi: काल के साथ लेखों में पश्चिमी क्षत्रपों के उषवदत्त के उपहार दर्ज हुए, दिखाते हुए कि नए शासक भी पुराने बौद्ध स्थलों को मान देते थे।

panels.shot: solemn mid-shot of a Satavahana representative making a donation before monks, royal seal on a document visible
panels.action: Within the hall, a dignified envoy bearing the insignia of Vasisthiputra Pulumavi presents a formal grant to the monks, beside a pillar ready to receive another inscription.

dialogue.text: Another inscription names Vasisthiputra Pulumavi of the Satavahanas, revealing how different dynasties, Satrap and Satavahana, turned to the same sanctuary as donors.

i18n.hi: एक और लेख में सातवाहनों के वशिष्ठिपुत्र पुलुमावि का नाम है, बताता है कि क्षत्रप और सातवाहन जैसी अलग वंशावलियाँ भी एक ही तीर्थ पर दाता बनकर आईं।

panels.shot: wide composite shot inside the hall, pillars marked with older merchant names and later royal ones, monks moving in the background
panels.action: The hall glows in soft light, its pillars bearing a tapestry of names—from early merchants and Yavanas to later Satrap and Satavahana donors—as monks move in quiet routine.

dialogue.text: Karla’s stone remembers both caravans and crowns, its walls stitched with merchant guilds, foreign donors and ruling houses who all sought lasting merit.

i18n.hi: कार्ला का पत्थर कारवाँ और मुकुट दोनों को याद रखता है, उसकी दीवारें व्यापार-श्रोतों, विदेशी दाताओं और राजघरानों की सिलाई से भरी हैं, जो सभी स्थायी पुण्य खोजने आए।

panels.shot: reflective close-up on the base of Bhutapala’s pillar inscription, weathered but legible, fingers of a modern visitor tracing the letters
panels.action: Centuries later, a modern visitor’s hand traces the worn Brahmi letters of Bhutapala’s claim, the old words faint yet still visible in the stone’s surface.

dialogue.text: Bhutapala’s boast of excellence was not a surveyor’s measure, but the voice of a proud banker, sure that his generosity carved greatness into the rock.

i18n.hi: भूतपाल की ‘श्रेष्ठता’ कोई नाप-जोख नहीं, बल्कि एक गर्वीले बैंकर की आवाज थी, यकीन से भरी कि उसकी उदारता ने ही चट्टान में महानता तराशी।

panels.shot: final sweeping interior wide, camera looking down the axis of the hall toward the stupa, shafts of light catching dust motes above a quiet monk
panels.action: A lone monk sits in meditation before the stupa as sunlight filters through the great doorway, revealing the stone ribs and inscribed pillars rising like timeless witnesses around him.

dialogue.text: Karla’s great chaitya still stands, a stone ship of faith hewn by workshops, guilds and distant Yavanas, proving that shared devotion and trade can cut lasting beauty from the heart of a mountain.

i18n.hi: कार्ला का महान चैत्य आज भी खड़ा है, आस्था का पत्थर-जहाज़, जिसे कारीगरों, श्रोतों और दूर के यवनों ने गढ़ा, साबित करते हुए कि साझा भक्ति और व्यापार मिलकर पहाड़ के दिल से टिकाऊ सुंदरता काट सकते हैं।

subtitle_i18n.en: Bhutapala’s Stone Mansion and the Merchants of the Western Sea
subtitle_i18n.hi: भूतपाल का पत्थर-महल और पश्चिमी सागर के व्यापारी
